symbols.name: coefficient index
symbols.meaning: The index running over the $r$ coefficient positions of a polynomial in the ring, $0 \le j < r$.
symbols.quote: The index $j$ runs over the $r$ coefficient positions, $0 \le j < r$.

symbols.name: packed polynomial
symbols.meaning: An element of the ring whose integer coefficients $f_j$ are packed into an integer.
symbols.quote: Take elements $f$ and $g$ of the ring with integer coefficients $f_j$ and $g_j$.

symbols.name: second polynomial
symbols.meaning: A second element of the ring with integer coefficients $g_j$, packed in the same way as $f$.
symbols.quote: Take elements $f$ and $g$ of the ring with integer coefficients $f_j$ and $g_j$.

symbols.name: coefficient bound
symbols.meaning: A bound on the absolute value of every coefficient of $f$ and $g$.
symbols.quote: Let $M$ be a bound on the absolute value of every such coefficient.

symbols.name: packing base
symbols.meaning: The power of two at which polynomials are evaluated to pack them into integers.
symbols.quote: Fix a power of two $B$ with $B > 2rM^2$, and call $B$ the packing base.

symbols.name: packed integer of f
symbols.meaning: The integer obtained by evaluating $f$ at the packing base $B$.
symbols.quote: The packed integer of $f$ is $F = \sum_j f_j B^j$, which may be negative because the digits are signed.

symbols.name: packed integer of g
symbols.meaning: The integer obtained by evaluating $g$ at the packing base $B$.
symbols.quote: Packing $g$ in the same way gives the integer $G = \sum_j g_j B^j$.

symbols.name: unreduced product
symbols.meaning: The product $fg$ of $f$ and $g$ as polynomials, before reduction modulo $y^r+1$.
symbols.quote: Let $h = fg$ be the unreduced product, with coefficients $h_k = \sum_j f_j g_{k-j}$, summed over all valid $j$, where $k$ is the power of $y$.

symbols.name: product power
symbols.meaning: The power of $y$ indexing a coefficient $h_k$ of the unreduced product.
symbols.quote: Let $h = fg$ be the unreduced product, with coefficients $h_k = \sum_j f_j g_{k-j}$, summed over all valid $j$, where $k$ is the power of $y$.

relations.quote: Signed Kronecker packing maps each element of [Polynomial ring modulo yʳ + 1](polynomial-ring-y.md) to a single integer, by evaluating it at a large power of two.

Signed Kronecker packing is an instance of [Multiplication as convolution of digits](convolution-reduction.md): the coefficients play the role of digits, and the evaluation point plays the role of the radix.
